title: Perplexity Open-Sources SPACE, a Firecracker MicroVM Sandbox for AI Agents
source_used: TokenPost, BigGo Finance and Forkast News (MarkTechPost blocked)
key_facts: Perplexity open-sourced SPACE (Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution) on 15 Oct 2026 under the Apache 2.0 licence; it is written in Rust.
Each agent task runs in its own Firecracker microVM; API keys stay outside each VM and external traffic goes through a gateway.
SPACE can save a VM's memory, running state and files so tasks can pause, resume or branch from a saved point.
Perplexity replaced its previous commercial sandbox service with SPACE in July 2026; it creates millions of sandboxes a day and median creation time fell from 185 to 60 milliseconds.

In security tests nine frontier models tried to break out; BigGo reports zero VM-to-host escapes in 108 attempts, Forkast about 118; some network-restriction bypasses were found and the company says they are patched.
CoreWeave and Akamai are testing and running SPACE and Crusoe has a partnership to add it to its managed AI services.
Nvidia's OpenShell is another open-source agent sandbox.
quote_evidence: SPACE powers Perplexity’s Computer product and uses Firecracker to create a separate microVM for every agent task.
The company says these have been patched, and the exploits no longer succeed in retesting.
In July 2026, Perplexity replaced its previous commercial sandbox service with SPACE.
why_it_matters_hint: A free, production-used way to contain AI agents, though the security results are the company's own.
notes: Older news re-dated: released 15 Oct, already in the 16 Oct edition. Attempt count differs between outlets.
